analysis.title: US Digital Ad Q3'26 Preview: Analyzing the Industry Debates & Framing the Operating Environment
key_insights: GS channel checks show a resilient digital ad environment with solid to strong momentum exiting Q3 2026, strongest among the larger scaled platforms in coverage.

AI is becoming the primary structural driver of digital ad share gains. Platforms that pair proprietary intent data with end-to-end automation (retrieval, bidding, creative assembly) are capturing a growing share of incremental budgets, and GS expects this to build into 2027 budget allocation.

Direct response (performance) advertising remains structurally stronger than top-of-funnel brand advertising. Brand stayed weaker than direct response despite easier year-over-year comps, and the World Cup gave only episodic brand lifts with limited visibility on durability.

Vertical trends: strongest in commerce/retail (more AI experimentation, budgets spread across more impressions), travel (normal summer seasonality) and autos (shift toward connected TV). Consumer electronics was strong as companies spent on marketing after component-cost price increases, and Q4 durability at higher prices is an open question.
Budget visibility has shortened as advertisers watch the consumer and macro backdrop, which could produce neutral to conservative holiday commentary in the coming earnings season.

The US is a relative area of strength given a strong consumer and midterm election spending. Political advertising is running above historical election cycles and is adding pricing pressure across September and October.
Smaller platforms face growing pressure to differentiate as scaled platforms broaden AI/ML ad offerings and push measurability in direct response.
Q3 pricing rose sequentially across digital advertising as AI/ML-driven ROAS gains show up in higher auction pricing. Gupta Media data shows average US Meta CPMs up ~8% QoQ and ~21% YoY.
Instagram CPMs in Q3: Feed +25% YoY (+9% QoQ), Stories +40% YoY (+9% QoQ), Reels +27% YoY (-8% QoQ). Meta US and global CPMs are tracking at ~1.5-2.5x and ~3-5x Q3 2019 levels.

SensorTower data shows US user growth and time spent stable, international stronger, with a slight deceleration toward the end of Q3. Pinterest, Reddit, Instagram and Snapchat had the strongest global MAU growth (+15%, +6%, +4%, +4% YoY).

Short-form video keeps driving engagement. Instagram averages ~58 minutes a day in the US, YouTube ~84 minutes, and TikTok ~80 minutes (down from a ~92 minute peak in mid 2023). Reels reached ~51% of Instagram US user time and ~55% of ads served in Q2'26.

Agentic commerce is the key extension of the AI debate. Consumer agents (Meta Muse, Google Universal Cart, LLM commerce integrations) compress discovery, comparison and checkout into one surface. Platforms need to capture transaction attribution and intent before queries migrate away from search. GS has not seen the final form of platform competition.

Meta Muse passed 9mm global downloads and 2mm+ daily active users as of 10/11 since its September launch. GS treats it as early in its product evolution, with debates on engagement durability, breadth of use cases and product-market fit.
Consumer AI chatbots are becoming ad-supported. Brands initially treat these impressions as middle-funnel discovery formats, not conversion formats, and worry about eroding trust in LLM answers.

Industry event takeaways: AI is changing consumer behavior, AI workflow automation improves performance and not just efficiency, full-funnel strategies produce the best results, micro-creators dominate discovery, and unique first-party data and signal drive outsized AI performance.

Meta disclosed that advertisers with diverse creative assets see on average +32% efficiency and +9% incremental reach. Meta Data Connectors aims to give agents structured, governed access to enterprise context.

Creators are treated as mainstream premium inventory. eMarketer estimates 45% of creator-focused brand spend goes to influencers with under 20k followers, with monetization shifting from brand-direct deals toward affiliate models.

Alphabet and Meta debates center on AI capex and capital intensity, funding needs and positioning in consumer agents. Investors are more comfortable with current-period ROIC, but the revenue and EBIT needed in 2028-2030 to earn returns on 2026/2027 capex remain questioned.

Alphabet (Buy, $435 PT unchanged): near-term worries are Search growth and no formal consumer agent launch yet versus Meta Muse. GS sees a possible consumer agent launch alongside Gemini 4 before the holidays and Google Cloud revenue reacceleration as constructive catalysts.

Meta (Buy, PT raised to $860 from $725): shares are up 37% from August lows on the Muse agent and Wonder model launches. GS forecasts 2027 opex above the Street and raises 2028E capex and opex while lowering 2029-31E capex, expecting AI infrastructure spend to be pulled forward into the next 18-24 months.

GS Meta Q3 revenue estimate is $63.7bn (+24.3% YoY, 0.5% above consensus, guidance $61-64bn). GS 2027 operating income is $92.4bn, 10.7% below consensus of $103.5bn, because of higher expenses (9.1% above consensus) and capex (13.1% above).

GS Alphabet estimates are unchanged apart from share count. GS 2027 Google Cloud revenue is $187.5bn (4.0% above consensus) but Cloud operating income is 11.9% below consensus, and total 2027 GAAP operating income is 5.3% above consensus. Q3 Google Search & Other is 1.1% below consensus.
GS Alphabet capex forecast: $203bn in 2026E (+122% y/y) and $350bn in 2027E (+72%), capital intensity of 47% and 64% of net revenue.

AppLovin (Neutral): PT cut to $400 from $465 as GS lowers multiples (14.5x EV/EBITDA from 17.0x, 15.0x EV/FCF-SBC from 17.0x) and trims out-year gaming growth. GS 2027 revenue is 3.3% below consensus and 2027 adj. EBITDA 4.6% below.

Liftoff Mobile (Buy): PT cut to $26 from $38 on lower multiples (5.0x EV/Sales from 7.0x, 9.5x EV/EBITDA from 12.5x) and slightly lower 2027+ growth for the in-app ad market. Q3 revenue estimate $221mm sits within the $217-222m guide.
Ethos (LIFE, Buy): PT raised to $43 from $35. GS raises 2027 revenue to $936mm from $833mm and 2027 adj. EBITDA to $181mm from $149mm. The Q3 activated-policy estimate was cut 8% and ARPU raised 9%.

MediaAlpha (Neutral): PT cut to $10.50 from $14 and valuation method moved to a 'mature' company framework (8.0x EV/GAAP EBITDA) as the P&C insurance cycle ages. The company pre-announced Q3 revenue and adj. EBITDA at or above guidance.
Yelp (Neutral): PT cut to $24 from $26 on a 5.5x EV/EBITDA multiple (3-year average). GS 2027 adj. EBITDA is 6% below consensus.
Ibotta (Sell): PT raised to $35 from $32 on lower 2027+ S&M expense and a higher EV/EBITDA multiple (17.0x). The stock at $42.96 is 19% above the target.
Pinterest (Buy, $30 PT unchanged): GS Q3 adj. EPS $0.47 is 20% below consensus of $0.58, with revenue in line at $1,205mm. 2027 adj. EBITDA is 5% above consensus.
Unity (Neutral, $50 unchanged): GS 2027 revenue is 5% and adj. EBITDA 12% above consensus.
Reddit (Neutral, $215 unchanged): GS Q3 revenue $868mm sits in the $860-870m guide. GS 2027 US revenue is 4% below consensus.
Snap (Neutral, $6.50 unchanged) trades at $6.53, so the target implies 0% upside. GS 2027 adj. EBITDA is 6% below consensus.

risk_factors: Consumer electronics demand durability at higher component-cost-driven prices is an open question for Q4.
Shorter advertiser budget duration and macro caution could lead to neutral or conservative holiday commentary.
Brand advertising durability after the World Cup and other summer sporting events is uncertain.
Political ad spending is raising ad prices in September and October, which could crowd out or distort other demand.
Alphabet and Meta: AI capex intensity, possible funding needs, and returns on 2026/2027 capex that depend on 2028-2030 revenue and EBIT.
Alphabet could lose Search share if consumer behavior migrates to agentic interfaces before it launches a consumer agent.
Meta Muse engagement durability, breadth of use cases and product-market fit are unproven.
Agentic commerce faces friction from data and app integration, trust and safety, and consumer adoption.
Erosion of third-party data and tighter privacy regulation.
Regulatory and antitrust scrutiny of large platforms.

Exhibit 12 and 13 show Instagram US user time spent and ads shown by surface, and the text states Reels at ~51% of time and ~55% of ads in Q2'26.
Exhibit 14 and 15 show Muse US DAUs and global downloads since launch, and the text states Muse at 2mm+ DAUs and 9mm downloads.

tension_points.bull_case: Integrated tech stack, Google Cloud reacceleration with strong profits, and a possible consumer agent launch alongside Gemini 4 before the holidays could improve the near-term narrative.
tension_points.bear_case: Investor concerns on Search revenue growth, no formal consumer agent launch yet to counter Meta Muse, and Alphabet's search positioning if consumer behavior migrates toward agentic interfaces.

tension_points.bull_case: Investors have grown more comfortable with current-period ROIC on prior spending, supported by Google Cloud growth and Meta product innovation.
tension_points.bear_case: Questions remain about the revenue and EBIT contribution needed in 2028-2030 to generate sufficient returns on 2026/2027 capex levels.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Revenue and EBIT contribution in 2028-2030 failing to reach the levels needed to earn returns on 2026/2027 capex.

tension_points.bull_case: Muse passed 9mm downloads and 2mm+ DAUs, and supports a conversation-to-action shift that connects frontier models with consumer monetization.
tension_points.bear_case: Muse is early in its product evolution, with open debates on engagement durability, breadth of use cases and evidence of product-market fit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence that Muse engagement fails to persist as the initial launch period matures.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 ad demand was resilient with strong exit momentum, led by retail, travel, autos and consumer electronics.
tension_points.bear_case: Shorter budget duration, caution on the consumer and macro backdrop, and uncertain consumer electronics demand at higher prices point to conservative Q4 commentary.
